correctness.rationale: For norm-one PSD matrices, p(t)=2(1+sqrt(2))-4t is strictly positive, and t-1/p(t) is concave with signed contacts -E,+E,-E at t=0,1/sqrt(2),1, proving a uniform matrix-functional-calculus bound E=(sqrt(2)-1)/2. For A=diag(0,1/sqrt(2),1) and squared component weights sqrt(2)-1,sqrt(2),1, the residual-square minus E^2 iterate-square is exactly a quadratic in affine polynomial coefficients with leading minor 3-sqrt(2)>0 and determinant (3sqrt(2)-4)/8>0; its unique zero is the constructive p. Thus the lower bound holds for ALL affine polynomials, and the upper bound is attained. Strict quadratic positivity for each smaller constant survives SPD perturbation of the zero eigenvalue, proving the limiting SPD supremum. Exact identities were rerun with the included SymPy file; random tests supplement but do not establish the theorem.

originality.rationale: The inspected motivating 2026 paper bounds the ideal MINBERR backward error by 3/(k^2-1); for k=2 this equals 1, not the attained exact worst-case factor (sqrt(2)-1)/2. Its polynomial approximation step supplies the known method of finding universal UPPER bounds, whereas the three-mode spectral-weight lower-bound certificate and sharp finite-step algorithmic value are not stated. Levin and Saff (1988) prove rate estimates for polynomial reciprocals; their Theorem 2.3 does not state the weighted MINBERR sharp threshold. Binh Lam (1976) describes exact rational Chebyshev errors and may include the scalar approximation constant; the claim is strictly the worst-case optimization value and matched matrix/vector witness, not priority for scalar approximation itself. Source comparisons and mathematical-record searches disclosed no covering algorithmic theorem, but publication priority is not independently certified.
residual_risks: The 1976 Binh Lam full text and some older equivalent approximation calculations were unavailable; priority for the scalar reciprocal-affine constant is not asserted.
Semantic searches of mathematical records and published sources cannot rule out unindexed equivalent results or stronger abstract duality formulations.
The witness uses a singular inconsistent system; the positive-definite extremal value is a supremum approached as the smallest eigenvalue tends to zero.

value.rationale: The motivating general MINBERR estimate at two Krylov vectors only yields a backward-error factor of 1. The new exact attained factor about 0.2071 is substantially sharper, directly operational for stopping and method comparison. The critical three-point positive spectral measure proves that the reciprocal polynomial estimate is not an artificial analysis artifact, and the SPD limiting result shows relevance to arbitrarily ill-conditioned consistent systems. A rigorous exact finite-step sharp benchmark is useful even without a new all-k convergence theorem.
